record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Is the oscillatory integer sequence [n sin n] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Show that the sequence ([n sin n]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\lfloor x \rfloor$ denote the integer part of a real number $x$, and consider the integer sequence $a(n) = \lfloor n \sin n \rfloor$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

A sequence of integers $(a(n))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is said to be good for multiple recurrence (for powers of a single transformation) if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$, every integer $k \geq 1$, and every set $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A \cap T^{-a(n)} A \cap T^{-2 a(n)} A \cap \cdots \cap T^{-k a(n)} A\bigr) > 0.$$

The sequence is said to be good for multiple convergence (of powers of a single transformation) if for every such system $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$, every $k \geq 1$, and all bounded measurable functions $f_1, \ldots, f_k \in L^\infty(\mu)$, the multiple ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{a(n)} x) \cdot f_2(T^{2 a(n)} x) \cdots f_k(T^{k a(n)} x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N \to \infty$.

Question: Is the sequence $(\lfloor n \sin n \rfloor)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ good for multiple recurrence and for multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation?
artifact.status_search_result: The sequence $\lfloor n \sin n \rfloor$ does not belong to a Hardy field (since $\sin n$ is not in a Hardy field), so it falls outside the scope of recent results on multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy-field sequences of polynomial growth (Frantzikinakis et al.). No source located in the search resolves this specific oscillatory sequence, and the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy sequences of polynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy field sequences of polynomial growth, but $n \sin n$ is not a Hardy field function.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results cover Hardy-field sequences and do not address $\lfloor n\sin n\rfloor$.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) extensions to Hardy field functions; the sequence n sin n is not in a Hardy field.
status_evidence.claim: Recent advances cover Hardy-field functions but not oscillatory sequences like n sin n.
